resources.string: Multiple devices shoot automatically at the same still moment, round after round
Each device in a session needs a different name
On another device, tap “Host a Session”, and keep both devices on the same Wi‑Fi or hotspot

This is your first time joining this host. Once joined, the host can fire this device\'s shutter, change its capture settings, and see its device name, battery, free storage and other status. Photos stay on this device and are never sent to the host. You won\'t be asked again when rejoining this host.
Couldn\'t connect to the host. Please try again.
Team up several phones and expose together at the same agreed moment
Shoots only when every device is steady—less blur, no tapping shot by shot
Each photo carries capture time, exposure, attitude and more for 3D Gaussian Splatting and other reconstruction
Team Up on the Same Network
One device hosts, the others tap “Join Session”
Put the devices on the same Wi‑Fi (or one phone\'s hotspot) and they find the host automatically—no QR codes
Android and iPhone can share a session, and either can be the host
Everything runs on the devices. Photos stay on each device and are never uploaded
Optional permissions aren\'t required, and you can change them later in system settings

Turn on the camera and Bluetooth. On first connection the camera shows a pairing code; check that it matches, then confirm on the camera.
Menu → Network → Bluetooth: turn on “Bluetooth Function” and “Bluetooth Rmt Ctrl”, then go to “Pairing”. When the phone shows a Bluetooth pairing request, tap “Pair”.

Menu → Wireless settings → Bluetooth function: choose “Remote” (BR-E1 compatible) or “Smartphone”, then start pairing. When the phone shows a Bluetooth pairing request, tap “Pair”; in Smartphone mode, also confirm on the camera.
Settings → Connection Setting → Bluetooth Settings → Pairing Registration. When the phone shows a Bluetooth pairing request, tap “Pair”.
Setup menu → Bluetooth remote control (ML-L7) → Pairing. “Smart device” mode needs Classic Bluetooth, which the app can\'t use.
Menu → Bluetooth → Pairing (GR III / IIIx / IV). When the phone shows a Bluetooth pairing request, check the number, then tap “Pair”.
Preferences → Connections → Connect Device → GoPro Quik App (HERO9 and later). When the phone shows a Bluetooth pairing request, tap “Pair”.
%1$s: connection was declined on the camera
%1$s is overheating and can\'t shoot for now
%1$s is asleep. Press any button on the camera to wake it.
The Bluetooth remote protocol only sends shutter commands. External cameras must be mounted on the same rig as the connected phone, or stillness detection won\'t work properly.
Each round, the cameras connected here fire together with this device\'s shutter.
Turn on Bluetooth on the camera and enter pairing mode (see below). Paired cameras reconnect automatically.

GoPro support is built on the Open GoPro specification. Sony, Canon, Fujifilm, Nikon and Ricoh protocols are ported from the open-source project gkoh/furble. Some brands haven\'t been tested on real hardware yet and may behave slightly differently.
Insta360 doesn\'t support a Bluetooth remote shutter, and its Wi‑Fi shutter control conflicts with this app, so there are no plans to support it for now.
Tap “Pair” in the Bluetooth pairing request on the phone, then confirm as prompted on the camera screen
Check the pairing code on the camera; if it matches, confirm on the camera
New number: %1$s. Trigger records use it starting with the next round, e.g. r0001_A01_%1$s.json.
The Nearby devices permission is needed to find and connect external cameras
Lead time offsets Bluetooth and camera latency; extra wait gives the camera time to save. External cameras must be mounted on the same rig as the phone.
Once external cameras are connected, trigger lead per brand appears here
External cameras connect through the Bluetooth remote channel, which only transmits shutter commands.
External cameras connected here can\'t detect stillness on their own; mount them on the same rig
Press any button on the camera to wake it; it resumes automatically. No shutter is sent while it\'s asleep.
Camera overheated; can\'t shoot for now
Sony, Canon, Fujifilm, Nikon, Ricoh: Bluetooth remote protocols ported from furble (MIT License); the Ricoh part references ricoh-gr-bluetooth-api.
DJI: based on the DJI R SDK protocol documentation and the Osmo GPS Controller Demo (DJI EULA; sample code also under the MIT License).
GoPro: based on the Open GoPro Bluetooth specification; interface constants follow the Open GoPro Python SDK (MIT License).
The brand names above are trademarks of their respective owners and are used only to describe compatibility. %1$s is not affiliated with, endorsed by, or sponsored by these companies.
Capture settings are controlled by the host; you can only view them here.
Opens straight into the host camera. To join as a client, tap × at the top left to leave, then choose “Join Session”.

Android devices take the frame closest to the agreed moment from a continuous stream; Quality First uses finer noise reduction and may lower the frame rate. RAW is saved as DNG; multi-lens capture and the zoomed telephoto don\'t shoot RAW. “RAW” (DNG only) is Android-only—iPhones shoot RAW + JPEG instead.
RAW wasn\'t captured this round; only the processed photo was saved
HEIC encoding failed; saved as JPEG instead: %1$s
The current lens setup can\'t shoot RAW (multi-lens, zoomed telephoto or unsupported lens); saving %1$s only
Takes effect only where each device allows the permission. Location is written only into the photos and never uploaded. Gyro data is saved as a JSON file with the photo\'s name.
Lock Focus keeps the current focus position. For 3DGS, turning on all three is recommended. Long-press the viewfinder to lock all camera settings.
Off: stillness isn\'t checked; shots are taken at the minimum interval no matter how much the devices move.
Host Gyro Only: doesn\'t wait for clients; all devices shoot as soon as the host is still.
If any device moved or missed the shot, the whole round is deleted.
If any device missed the shot, the whole round is deleted.
Codes are assigned in order; tap a device\'s code to change it. The code turns yellow when sync error exceeds 5 ms.
View photos taken on this device. Other devices keep their photos on their own storage; on iPhone, see the TuttiCam folder in the Files app.
Photos on this device are saved in %1$s. Tap to open it in Files.
No app can open this folder
Once you start shooting, photos will be organized by scene here
Only files on this device are deleted; other devices aren\'t affected. This can\'t be undone.
The RAW and metadata files with the same name will also be deleted. This can\'t be undone.
New code: %1$s. Photo file names use it from the next round.
